systemic.title: Plain dereferences of game memory
systemic.detail: Aligned loads and stores through integers cast to pointers. Undefined behaviour for any address that is not aligned at run time, and debug builds check alignment and panic. Build the injected library in release with debug assertions off until these are converted, or convert them to read_unaligned/write_unaligned (1046 files already do).

systemic.title: Integer overflow behaviour depends on the build profile
systemic.detail: The checker builds release, where + - * and shifts wrap as the original's do. A debug or overflow-checked build of the same code panics instead. Set overflow-checks = false for the library profile, or convert to wrapping operations.

issues.title: Doc says the vtable call goes through checker callee 1; code calls the slot directly
issues.detail: The comment names checker callee 1, but the code reads the slot at vtable+4 from game memory and calls it through a transmuted pointer; no callee slot is used. Behaviour is fine for production, the comment is wrong.

issues.title: Fetch-helper out-buffer sized 6 words; true descriptor size unconfirmed
issues.detail: The rewrite gives the descriptor-fill callee a 6-word stack buffer while other leaderboard siblings give 8. issues.title: Callee writes through a pointer derived from a shared reference to a by-value arg
issues.detail: The out-param pointer is made from a shared reference to the immutable parameter a4, and the callee may write through it, which is undefined behaviour in Rust. The comment also relies on rustc homing a4 in the incoming stack slot, which is codegen-dependent (inlining/LTO in a combined build can move it), so the proven stack-offset equality may not hold in production.

issues.title: Only AL compared; upper EAX bytes of the boolean return not proven
issues.detail: The comment states the contract compares only the al channel because the original leaves the upper EAX bytes as the caller had them; the rewrite returns a zero-extended u32. Fine for callers testing AL only, unproven for any caller reading the full register.

issues.title: Doc says byte 0x11 is left untouched, but the 16-bit store at 0x10 writes it
issues.detail: The comment lists 0x11 among the bytes not written, yet the code zeroes a u16 at offset 0x10, which covers 0x10 and 0x11.

issues.title: Four callee slots with no target named; sweep and tail call share slot 4
issues.detail: Callees 1-4 are identified neither by address nor by name in the file, so assembly cannot wire them; slot 4 serves both the per-slot sweep and the tail call on the object, which should be confirmed to be the same original target.

issues.title: Plain + on a pointer value read from a global
issues.detail: base + 0x44D uses checked addition, which panics in a debug build if the global holds a value near the top of the address space; the original wraps. Use wrapping_add.

issues.title: Virtual handler at vtable+0x1C invoked as cdecl with no object in ECX
issues.detail: The original ends in a computed jump through the chain object's vtable slot, which for a virtual method normally expects the object in ECX; the rewrite calls the target as a no-argument cdecl function so ECX is whatever the compiler left. Verify in game which register state the handler needs, and whether the checker compares ECX at this call.

issues.title: strlen helper indexes a 48-byte array and panics if no NUL was written
issues.detail: The local `strlen` walks `buf[i]` with checked indexing; if the real collector fills all 48 bytes without a terminator the rewrite panics (abort) where the original would read on. The doc asserts a NUL is always stored, which only the stub guarantees.

issues.title: Deliberately wrong 'honesty-mutant' count gate shipped in the verified file
issues.detail: `mut_count_gate` is the wrong version used for the mutant run; it is dead code in the tracked rewrite and could be called by mistake at assembly. Mutants belong in the contract, not the rewrite.

issues.title: Callees write through pointers derived from immutable locals (&tmp_a .. &tmp_e)
issues.detail: Out-parameter slots are immutable let bindings whose shared-reference address is handed to callees that fill them and return them, and the rewrite then reads the result back through that address; writing through a shared-reference-derived pointer is UB and the optimizer may assume the locals stay 0. Declare them mut and pass addr_of_mut!.

issues.title: Out-pointer to immutable local `tmp` handed to a callee that may write it
issues.detail: `tmp` is an immutable binding whose address is passed to callee 5 as what looks like an out-parameter; if the real callee writes it, that is a write through a shared-reference-derived pointer. Make it `mut` and use addr_of_mut!.

issues.title: Sample accepted when equal to the entry count (one past the last entry)
issues.detail: The bound check rejects only sample > count, so sample == count indexes the entry after the last. May mirror the original; verify in game. fn_008b75e0 has the same check and does not bound the third sample at all.

issues.title: Object pointer 0x0118D7F0 passed to the sensor callee without relocated()
issues.detail: The thiscall receiver is the raw file VA, whereas every sibling (fn_005b46a0, fn_008b82d0, fn_008b41b0) passes relocated(0x0118D7F0). In game this hands the callee a wrong object whenever the image is rebased, and the pass shows the checker did not compare this callee's ECX. Applies to fn_008b8ee0 too.

The rewrite calls it as a no-argument cdecl, so wired to the real check it sees garbage ECX and terminates the process. The cookie call should be dropped (Rust has its own stack protection) and the return value contract revisited.

issues.title: 32-wchar scratch buffer filled by an unbounded loader (-1); indexing panics
issues.detail: The loader is told the length is unlimited (0xFFFFFFFF) but `buf` holds only 32 u16s; a longer string overruns the Rust stack array, and the scan uses checked `buf[idx]`, which panics past 31 (also inside the skip loop, which does not stop at NUL). The original frame buffer is probably larger (it has a /GS cookie). Size it from the original frame.

issues.title: Virtual destructor called as stdcall(1) without the object in ECX

issues.title: Gather call's second argument passed as 0 where the original passes an uninitialised regis
issues.detail: Admitted in the doc; the contract does not compare it, so if the gather helper uses that word the in-game result differs.

issues.title: Checked + on address values (src, this_ptr)
issues.detail: Address arithmetic on src, this_ptr uses the plain + operator, which panics on overflow when overflow checks are on (debug or overflow-checks builds) where the original wraps; use wrapping_add to keep the original semantics in every profile.

issues.title: Element address computed with plain + and * on a count read from memory
issues.detail: obj + j * ELEM_SIZE uses unchecked arithmetic on an array count taken from obj-0x10; a corrupt or large count overflows and panics in a debug build where the original wraps.

issues.title: Stack check disabled; the spill into the caller's argument slot is not reproduced
issues.detail: The doc says the original writes the looked-up word into its incoming argument slot and that the stack comparison was switched off for this contract; any caller that reads that slot afterwards is not covered.

issues.title: Drain loop proven for at most one iteration
issues.detail: The file states that with scripted callee answers only zero or one pass is observable, so multi-node drains are unproven.

issues.title: Entry EAX pinned to 0; extra pushed word to allocator not reproduced
issues.detail: The flag-set path returns caller EAX residue in the original (pinned to 0 here), and the constant second word the original pushes to the allocator callee is uncompared and omitted; both are argued harmless but not proven.

issues.title: Checked + on address values (obj)
issues.detail: Address arithmetic on obj uses the plain + operator, which panics on overflow when overflow checks are on (debug or overflow-checks builds) where the original wraps; use wrapping_add to keep the original semantics in every profile.

issues.title: Immutable zeroed arrays passed as frame blocks that callees may write
issues.detail: blk_a..blk_d are immutable bindings whose as_ptr() goes to the setup/item callees, which take frame blocks in the original (left uncompared); a callee writing through them mutates an immutable Rust local (UB), and an 8-word size is assumed rather than known. Declare them mut with the original's block size.

issues.title: Stack comparison switched off for this contract
issues.detail: The original spills the current object into its incoming argument slot and passes that address to the matcher; the rewrite uses a local, so the stack check was disabled and any effect on the caller's argument slot is unproven.

issues.title: Immutable arrays handed via as_ptr() to probe callees that fill them
issues.detail: `blk_a`/`blk_b` are immutable bindings; the doc calls the second callee a pair updater, so the real callee writes through a pointer derived from a shared borrow. Declare them mut and use as_mut_ptr().

issues.title: Callee output buffers declared as immutable locals and written through as_ptr
issues.detail: scratch (and possibly c16) are non-mut arrays whose addresses are handed to transform callees that write into them; writing through a pointer from a shared borrow is UB, so the optimiser may assume the contents are unchanged. Declare them mut and use as_mut_ptr.

issues.title: Two scratch words the original passes uninitialised are zeroed and left uncompared
issues.detail: The doc admits the contract excludes two words the original passes from uninitialised stack; the rewrite substitutes zeros.

issues.title: Transform output written into an immutable scratch array
issues.detail: scratch is an immutable [u32; 4] passed via as_ptr() to transform callee 3, which fills it before callee 4 reads it; writing through a pointer to an immutable local is UB and the compiler may assume it stays zero. Make it mut and use as_mut_ptr.

issues.title: Callee writes through block_a.as_ptr() (shared borrow); read_volatile papers over it
issues.detail: The tester writes its out-slot through a pointer obtained from as_ptr() on an array never mutably borrowed, which is undefined behaviour; the read_volatile exists precisely because the compiler may assume the value is unchanged. Use as_mut_ptr. Both blocks are also sized to the compared words only, so a real tester touching more of them reads/writes past the Rust arrays.

issues.title: Frame-cookie check called as no-argument cdecl
issues.detail: Callee 2 is the cookie check, called with no ECX setup; against the real check this fails and terminates the game. Drop it at assembly.

issues.title: Unbounded leg-name copy into a 12-byte tail of an 8-word Rust array
issues.detail: The leg name is strcpy'd into rec starting at word 5, leaving 12 bytes before the end of the 32-byte array; any name of 12+ characters overruns the Rust stack. The original's frame buffer is larger; the checker's short strings never reach the end.

issues.title: Fourth stored word is uninitialised stack in the original, zero in the rewrite
issues.detail: The doc states the original stores an uninitialised stack slot as the row's fourth word; the rewrite stores 0, which only matches under the contract's stack_fill.

issues.title: Doc says the level arrives on the x87 stack, but the code stores callee 3's EAX
issues.detail: The doc says the resulting level is delivered in ST0, yet the rewrite reads callee 3's answer as a u32 and stores it to the out-slot. A stub that answers the same value in EAX and ST0 passes the check, but the real callee leaves EAX undefined, so the stored level would be garbage in game. The fourth record word is also written as 0 where the original copies uninitialised stack.

issues.title: Coordinate passed by address is a lone copy of x; y and z arguments dropped
issues.detail: The original passes the address of its first coordinate stack argument, so the task builder reads x, y, z from three consecutive stack words; the rewrite copies only f1 into a single local and ignores _f2/_f3, so the real callee reads adjacent Rust stack for y and z. The pointer argument was necessarily masked, so the checker could not see this.

issues.title: Releases each slot through its vtable as stdcall(1) without passing the object
issues.detail: Slot 0 of the child's vtable (a scalar deleting destructor shape: flag 1) is called as stdcall with only the flag; the original almost certainly passes the child in ECX (thiscall). The checker compares no ECX for stdcall-declared callees, so in game the destructor runs on a garbage this.

issues.title: Virtual release called as stdcall(1) without the object in ECX
issues.detail: The held object's vtable slot 0 (its deleting destructor) is invoked as extern "stdcall" with only the flag 1; the object pointer is never passed, so in game the destructor runs on whatever ECX holds. Other rewrites in this family call the same slot as thiscall(object, 1). The planted checker stub evidently did not compare ECX.

issues.title: Gain-stage detach/silence callees get no object; declared stdcall
issues.detail: Callee 3 (silence with -4.0) receives only the gain value and callee 2 only this, although the operation targets the gain stage at +0x38; the real routines are likely thiscall on that object with ECX left from earlier code, which the contract did not compare. Verify the real conventions before wiring.

issues.title: Gain-stage silence/detach calls never pass the stage object
issues.detail: Callees 1 and 2 are declared stdcall and receive only the gain bits and this; the stage at +0x1C is never passed, so it presumably travels in ECX (thiscall) in the original, which the checker does not compare for stdcall callees. Wired to the real routines this operates on an arbitrary object.

issues.title: Subtask vf5 is called with zeros for its first two arguments
issues.detail: The rewrite forwards (0, 0, extra) to the subtask's slot +0x14, claiming the original's first two pushed words are an unobservable blend of return address and arg0; for a vf5-to-vf5 forward the natural arguments are (owner, kind, next), and the 'blend' reading looks like a misread of esp-relative pushes. The contract compares only the third word, so in game the subtask likely receives owner=0, kind=0. Verify in game.

In game the engine reads its triple through an arbitrary ECX: wrong values or a crash. Use a fastcall/thiscall-shaped call with ECX pointing at [arg4, arg5, arg6].
